questions.question_text: Read the unseen passage about the ancient banyan tree. According to the text, what primary benefit did the banyan tree provide to weary travelers during the scorching summer?
options: B) Cool, expansive shade for resting
C) Directions to the nearest village
questions.answer: B) Cool, expansive shade for resting

questions.question_text: Based on the passage context, select the most accurate synonym for the word 'resilience' as demonstrated by the tree during the storm.
questions.answer: C) Endurance

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank based on the passage: The little birds felt completely _________ when they nested deep within the tree's thick canopy.
questions.answer: B) secure

questions.question_text: Describe how the old banyan tree protected the little squirrel family during the heavy monsoon thunderstorm mentioned in the second paragraph. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: The banyan tree used its thick, broad leaves to form a natural waterproof umbrella, keeping the hollow trunk completely dry and safe for the trembling squirrel family.

questions.question_text: Why did the local villagers consider the ancient tree a profound symbol of unity and strength? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: The villagers viewed the tree as a symbol of unity because its numerous prop roots firmly anchored it to the ground, showing how standing together withstands life's harshest storms.

questions.question_text: In your own words, summarize the central theme or moral of this reading passage. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: The passage highlights that true strength lies in providing shelter and kindness to the vulnerable, just as the resilient tree protected all creatures without any discrimination.

sections.section_name: Section B - Writing Skills & Applied Grammar

questions.question_text: Identify the kind of noun for the highlighted word in the sentence: 'The young boy showed immense *courage* during the rescue.'
questions.answer: C) Abstract Noun

questions.question_text: Choose the correct reflexive pronoun to fill in the blank: 'The enthusiastic students painted the entire school mural by _________.'
questions.answer: A) themselves

questions.question_text: Select the correct comparative degree of the adjective to complete the sentence: 'This mathematical puzzle is _________ than the one we solved yesterday.'
questions.answer: B) more difficult

questions.question_text: Choose the appropriate article to fill in the blank: 'She is _________ honest leader who always speaks the truth to her followers.'
questions.answer: B) an

questions.question_text: Identify the main verb in the following sentence: 'The children were playing happily in the community garden.'
questions.answer: D) playing

questions.question_text: Choose the correct tense to complete the sentence: 'By this time next week, I _________ my science exhibition project.'
questions.answer: C) will have finished

questions.question_text: Identify the type of sentence based on its structure and purpose: 'Please pass me the salt from the dining table.'
questions.answer: C) Imperative

questions.question_text: Complete the sentence with the correct simple present tense verb: 'My grandfather always _________ to the local market every Sunday morning.'
questions.answer: D) goes

questions.question_text: Write a short descriptive paragraph on the topic 'The Importance of Reading Books'. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: Reading books is essential as it opens the doors to endless knowledge and imagination. It improves our vocabulary, sharpens our focus, and helps reduce stress by transporting us to different worlds. Books are our best companions, guiding us through life's challenges while continuously expanding our intellectual horizons.

questions.question_text: Write a diary entry expressing your feelings after winning the first prize in your school's inter-house debate competition. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: Dear Diary, Today was an unforgettable day! I won the first prize in the inter-house debate competition. When they announced my name, my heart skipped a beat with joy. All those late nights of researching and practicing finally paid off. My parents and teachers are so proud. I feel incredibly motivated!

questions.question_text: Read the extract from 'Paper Boats': "Day by day I float my paper boats one by one down the running stream." What specific detail does the child write on these boats?
options: B) His name and the name of his village
C) A poem about the river
questions.answer: B) His name and the name of his village

questions.question_text: Read the extract from 'Try Again': "If you find your task is hard..." What is the immediate advice given by the poet to complete this thought?
options: C) Time will bring you your reward, try again
questions.answer: C) Time will bring you your reward, try again

questions.question_text: In the lesson 'The Day the River Spoke', what significant event causes a change in the young protagonist's perspective of the river? [25-35 words]
questions.answer: The protagonist's perspective changes when she quietly sits by the bank and deeply observes the river's continuous, unstoppable flow. She realizes the river is a living, speaking entity offering timeless wisdom about life.

questions.question_text: According to the essay 'Three Days to See', what is the very first thing Helen Keller states she would want to see on her first day of sight? [25-35 words]
questions.answer: Helen Keller states that on the very first day, she would want to see the faces of the people whose kindness, gentle companionship, and deep love made her challenging life worth living.

questions.question_text: Describe the unique ability that made Dr. Dolittle entirely different from all other animal doctors in the story 'Animals Birds and Dr Dolittle'. [25-35 words]
questions.answer: Dr. Dolittle's unique ability was that he could actually learn and speak the secret languages of various animals, allowing him to communicate with them directly and understand their exact medical ailments.

questions.question_text: In the humorous story 'My Brothers Great Invention', what was the actual final outcome of the so-called brilliant mechanical invention? [25-35 words]
questions.answer: Instead of revolutionizing daily chores as he proudly promised, the brother's brilliant mechanical invention malfunctioned comically, creating a massive, noisy mess in the house and leaving everyone highly amused rather than helped.

questions.question_text: Analyze the central message conveyed by the poem 'Try Again', particularly detailing how one should face continuous setbacks and initial failures in life. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: The poem imparts a powerful motivational message: failure is not a disgrace but a stepping stone to eventual success. It teaches that continuous setbacks test our patience and courage. Instead of giving up in despair, we must muster our grit and try again, as sheer persistence always conquers difficult tasks.

questions.question_text: Discuss how the river is beautifully personified in 'The Day the River Spoke' and explain its deep impact on the young girl's understanding of nature. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: The river is personified as a wise, ancient storyteller whispering secrets of the earth. By 'speaking' to the girl, the river transforms from a mere body of water into a guiding friend. This deeply impacts her, helping her understand that nature possesses its own voice, spirit, and profound lessons for humanity.
